learning: Iteration 3 showed a forward offset of y = 0.07 m did not reduce line losses (1.0 per run on s-bend and slalom), and the controller held fixed in iterations 0 and 3 gave the best scores. The remaining untested single-variable lever is yaw inertia through mass. If line losses persist with max_error at or above 0.06 m, the next controller-independent test is body_length 0.12 m at 0.5 kg, one change at a time. Iteration 2's score is confounded and does not rule this out.
notes: Iteration 4 package: the Builder's iteration 4 geometry (mass 0.5 kg, sensor y 0.05 m, other fields unchanged from iteration 0) with the iteration 0 controller held exactly. Only mass differs from the best-scoring baseline, so the race isolates mass.
rationale: The evidence is three races, all with 0 of 60 completions and every run ending off track. Iteration 0 (score 63.0, the best) had max_error of 0.062 to 0.066 m and about 1.0 line-loss events per run on the s-bend and slalom, with steering_oscillation of only 0.13 to 0.15. The failure is one line loss followed by drift, not jitter. Iteration 1 showed that raising kp to 4.5 and kd to 0.3 on a 0.10 m track scored lower (53.7). Iteration 2 changed span, footprint, mass and body together and scored lowest (46.5). Iteration 3 moved the sensors to y = 0.07 m with the iteration 0 controller and scored 61.5, so the forward offset did not remove the line loss. This iteration the Builder asks for mass 0.7 to 0.5 kg with everything else unchanged from iteration 0. The controller is therefore kept exactly at the iteration 0 values (kp 3.0, ki 0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.5, last_direction, weights +1, +0.5, 0, -0.5, -1). No gain change is justified, because the only controller-gain test (iteration 1) was confounded with a narrower track and scored lower. Holding the controller fixed means any score change is attributable to mass, which is what the Builder is testing. The sensor offset is set to y = 0.05 m as the Builder requests, since iteration 3 showed the offset is not the limiting factor. Geometry values are passed through as proposed. Expected result: line losses near 1.0 or lower, max_error near 0.06 m, and a score near the iteration 0 level of 63. This is a prediction only.
